To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ECM, cytokines, proteolytic enzymes, and their interrelationships have a specialized role in coordinating leukocyte actions during inflammation.
the extracellular matrix is a dynamic, active component of the inflammatory response, and is capable of regulating the behavior of immune cells through its interactions with enzymes and cytokines.

1) cytokines and enzymes can modulate the adhesive and migratory behavior of leukocytes, 2) cytokine-ECM interactions may be critical for the regulation of leukocyte behavior, and 3) the ECM may provide a specialized niche for cytokines and degrada- tive enzymes that is critical for the regulation and perpetuation of inflammatory events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that regulate leukocyte behavior during inflammation.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that govern the behavior of leukocytes during inflammation.
the mechanisms by which the ECM and cytokines influence immune cell behavior and the inflammatory process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in addition to the well-known roles played by the ECM, cytokines, proteases, and integrins, the ECM micro-environment also provides signals to regulate the behavior of immune cells.
the ECM is a dynamic structure that can be modified by inflammatory cells and cytokines.

, in the context of inflammation, the ECM is not simply a scaffold for leukocyte adhesion and migration, but is a dynamic microenvironment that is actively engaged in orchestrating the inflammatory response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ECM is an integral component of the inflammatory response and, through its interactions and cross-talk with cytokines and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), it plays an active role in regulating the behavior of leukocytes and their effector functions during inflammation.
the ECM is a complex mixture of macromolecules that can influence leukocyte behavior and function in a dynamic manner.
the ECM is not merely a scaffold, but a dynamic, active, and instructive participant in regulating immune cell behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ECM molecules, cytokines, proteases, and their products are dynamic components of the inflammatory response that interact with each other to regulate the behavior of immune cells and the perpetuation or resolution of inflammation.
the ECM is not just a passive scaffold for cells, but rather it has a dynamic role in modulating cell behavior during inflammation.
the extracellular matrix is a dynamic structure that can change in response to the presence of cytokines and enzymes.
